metadata.name: Hunt and Hess Scale for Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
metadata.summary: 5-grade clinical classification of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage severity.
clinical_pearls: Original Hunt & Hess criteria add +1 grade for serious systemic disease (e.g., severe HTN, diabetes, COPD) or severe angiographic vasospasm.

options.label: Asymptomatic, or minimal headache and slight nuchal rigidity
Moderate-to-severe headache, nuchal rigidity, no neurological deficit other than cranial nerve palsy
Drowsiness, confusion, or mild focal neurological deficit
Stupor, moderate-to-severe hemiparesis, possible early decerebrate rigidity
Deep coma, decerebrate rigidity, moribund appearance

interpretation.label: Good Clinical Grade (I–II)
interpretation.summary: Alert without encephalopathy or limb weakness.

interpretation.label: Poor Clinical Grade (IV–V)
interpretation.summary: Stupor or coma; urgent ICU stabilization and ICP/hydrocephalus evaluation.

assessment_guides.title: Hunt & Hess Grade II vs Grade III
bedside_steps: Check alertness and screen for cranial nerve palsies vs limb motor/sensory/speech deficits.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Isolated cranial nerve palsy (e.g., CN III) remains Grade II if the patient is fully alert.
Any drowsiness/confusion or mild focal limb/language deficit upgrades to Grade III.

references.citation: Hunt WE, Hess RM. Surgical risk as related to time of intervention in the repair of intracranial aneurysms. J Neurosurg. 1968;28(1):14-20.
